title: Hierarchical Clustering
description: Clustering method building a tree of clusters via agglomerative or divisive merging.
name: Hierarchical Clustering
summary: Hierarchical Clustering groups data objects into a tree structure (dendrogram). Agglomerative clustering starts with each point as a separate cluster and merges them pair-by-pair based on linkage criteria.
use_when: Visualizing cluster hierarchies or needing to determine the optimal number of clusters via a dendrogram.
avoid_when: Dataset scales to tens of thousands of samples, as complexity scales cubically O(N^3).
pros: Produces a tree/dendrogram showing exact cluster relationships.
Does not require pre-specifying the number of clusters upfront.
Supports flexible linkage criteria (Ward, complete, average) to handle different shape types.
cons: Extremely expensive scaling O(N^3) time complexity and O(N^2) space complexity.
Once a step/merge is completed, it cannot be undone or reevaluated.
Sensitive to outliers which can form long isolated branches.

key_hyperparams.name: linkage
key_hyperparams.note: Which linkage criterion to use. Ward minimizes variance of merged clusters.

quick_start:
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[1, 2], [1, 4], [1, 0], [4, 2], [4, 4], [4, 0]])
clustering = AgglomerativeClustering().fit(X)
labels = clustering.labels_
